utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of weapons were being used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know, that those were automatic weapons; but what kind of, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when that shooting occurred, were the bullets able to pierce through the metal of this hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what was the purpose of the shooting into the hangar by those on the outside was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to intimidate us, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you or any of the other people in your hangar injured by any of the bullets or the metal that was then flying around after this shooting occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about your own injury.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A slight injury in the buttock. It wasn't serious. But three men around me sustained injuries, one on the temple and one on the arm, and the third was hit in the spine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you or the others receive any medical treatment for those injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing from outside except Dr. Eso Boskailo who was inside. He had some painkillers, and those three took those medicines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this doctor whom you've mentioned, is this someone who was made available to you by the authorities in the camp or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was another prisoner from Trijebanj. He was a doctor on duty for soldiers who were on the front line at Trijebanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned at the beginning of your testimony that at the time you were arrested, there were other civilians who were arrested. I wanted to ask you whether you saw any civilians who were also prisoners inside the Dretelj camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you know any of those prisoners from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. My neighbours, my relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see any religious officials in the Dretelj camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes. I knew from before efendi Ahmet Alic, efendi Hasan, who was the main efendi in the municipality of Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask that we use the ELMO again and look Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. again at the photograph that you looked at already which was marked as Exhibit 21.8. While that's being arranged, Witness, let me ask you, do you know if other prisoners were being kept in other buildings in the Dretelj camp during the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And it may be necessary for you to take that photograph back into your hand and then we'll put it on the ELMO again, but I want to ask you, in this photograph, just going down a bit from the hangar that you've circled, there appears to be another building that is partially underground, and I wonder if you can -- if you can point to that building for me so that we know that we're talking about the same one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. Going back to your hangar, the hangar that you were in, and then moving down toward the bottom of the photograph and toward the right a little bit. I'm sorry. Let me -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm having difficulty with this, Mr. President. Let me move ahead, and I think that I'll be able to make the connection. At this point, I'd ask that we look at a videotape which the Trial Chamber has not seen previously. It's Exhibit 23. It's a short videotape footage, lasting about, I think, a minute and a half, which was obtained from Danish television.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you to just simply look at the video, and then, after we've all looked at it, I'm going to ask you one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe somebody could turn the lights down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We've already seen basically the most important part. Perhaps since it's so short, I could ask we rewind so that we can all look at it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, going back to the photograph which is marked as Exhibit 21.8, are you able to point out for us the location, if you can, of the place that we just saw in the videotape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And perhaps for the record, I ask the witness be given a marker and he can place a circle around that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you, just looking at this photograph, are there two buildings such as that which appear to be facing each other across a concrete courtyard or pista in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, while you were being held at the Dretelj camp, did you see or were you aware of prisoners being held in these other buildings that now we've described or talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And finally, in the videotape that we just saw, did you see any people whom you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And perhaps with the Court's permission, we could play it one last time. I think we could fast forward, and I can tell them when to slow down or to stop, and if we could turn the lights down again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll watch the video once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Stop there, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, is this the person that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmet Alic, the imam.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, one last question about the videotape. Does it appear to depict accurately the conditions, as far as you recall them, that existed in the camp at Dretelj during the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. Yes. I can see a person who is 15 kilogrammes lighter, and others lost weight too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. We have finished with the videotape and we can now move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified, then, on the 21st of July, you were moved to a different place, or that you left Dretelj. Could you tell us, then, where you went on the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the Heliodrom with some other 400 or so persons. We were transferred in civilian trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And these other persons, were they prisoners, like you, at the Dretelj camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, from your arrival in the Heliodrom on the 21st of July, '93, can you tell us how long you remained, then, detained at the Heliodrom until you were released or moved to the next place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th of December, that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So, now I'm going to ask you a series of questions about things that occurred during those months you spent as a prisoner at the Heliodrom. First of all, could you tell us what happened when you arrived at the Heliodrom, and where you stayed or where you were placed upon your arrival.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the first four days in the school building, and the rest of the time in the gymnasium which adjoined the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll ask that the witness be shown Exhibit Number 20.8 which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in this photograph, are you able to recognise any of the places where you were detained or held when you were at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the school building where I spent four days. And these are two halls where prisoners were transferred because we were just too many in the school building. And I slept in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, if I could ask you, if you could take the photo with the pen, place a circle around the school building that you remained at for the first four days, and then maybe place a number "1" inside that circle. And then if you would circle, then, the second place where you were held for the longer period, which I believe you called the gymnasium or the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you place a number "2" in that one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Very good. Thank you. Witness, let me ask you, while you were in the Heliodrom, did you see or have contact with any soldiers who were also staying in the Heliodrom complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand "soldier." What soldier?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Maybe it was a bad question, and I'll try and ask a better one. Did you or the other prisoners have contact with soldiers from any different units or armies, not army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but of any other armies or units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who were those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was military police, they guarded us. And behind them here, there was a group. Now, how many of them -- there was a group, and they were introduced to us, the detainees. When they would bring us bread leftover after their meals, they would introduce themselves as Tigers or Thunderbolts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what armies those soldiers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that they were Tigers and Thunderbolts from the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You said that they left you extra bread. How did these soldiers treat you and the other prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had only come to the bars on the windows; and through the bars, they would give us bread. And they sometimes took out some prisoners to play basketball with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the time that you were being held at the Heliodrom, were you taken out of the Heliodrom to perform forced labour at different locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you recall, what groups or units that you worked for at the various times that you were taken out to perform forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked at the Bakina Luka. I worked in Zenica, in Rodoc, the 9th Battalion. I worked at Podhum, the 4th Battalion. I worked at Santiceva Street. I worked for ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How often did you work for ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would go there together with a group of some 30 of us who went there almost every day for some two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, who, if you know, was the commander of what you've called ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vinko Marinkovic [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How would you be taken out of the Heliodrom to the ATG Mrmak? How were you transported?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would go in a truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the people who would be the drivers who would transport you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Dinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Dinko a member of the ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a bit late since we've moved on, but Mr. President, it was a leading question. I think it should have been phrased differently, that is, whether the witness knew to whom that man belonged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which question you are directed at. The question is:

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the people who would be the drivers who would transport you? Then the answer is:

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Dinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Dinko a member of the ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the driver. Well, I don't think that is a leading question, Mr. Seric. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can recall approximately the month or the period of time when you started going to the ATG Mrmak, the beginning of this two-month period that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of August. The end of July, beginning of August. Some ten days after I arrived at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then during that next two-month period that you've described, how often did you go to ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost every day, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you were taken to the ATG Mrmak, can you describe the place or the location that you would be taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the road from the Bulevar which led towards the road going to Siroki Brijeg and Listica up there, leading out of town. Actually, from the Rondo. My mistake. From the Rondo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time, I would like to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 11.18, which is a map which should not contain any markings on it. We need a clean version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I know this is -- this size is a bit difficult to work with. Perhaps we could do it this way: Witness, let me first ask you to just take the map into your hand and take a look at it and get oriented, and then if you can, to take the pen and to place a mark with an "X" on the location that you are describing now as the location of ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now, while we're talking about that, tell us, please, tell the Judges, what was at this location that you've marked with an "X"? What was found there? When you would arrive, what did you find?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A house which had a basement and a first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how often were you taken to this house during this two-month Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. period that you've described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would spend most of my time during that period in the house and around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What purpose was that house being used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the headquarters, the command from where they went to the front line. From there, they went in all directions, depending on where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say it was the headquarters, just so we're clear, what headquarters are you talking about? Headquarters of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of which the commander was Mr. Vinko Martinovic, Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during these two months that you were taken to work at this place, how often did you see Stela, Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I must say that while I was there -- I was there almost every day and I spent almost all the time there, so I was in relatively close contact with Vinko Martinovic. I would make coffee, clean the premises, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who -- can you tell us, if you know, the names of other persons whom you encountered in that headquarters during those two months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Dubi, Dolma, Ernest Takac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. How often did you see this person you've called Ernest Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every day. He would come and go. He would pass by. He would stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brada, or beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that during the time you were in this house, you would make coffee, clean the premises, things like that. Were there other duties or tasks that you were given to perform during this two months that you were taken to this headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times, I would go to the front line. And if they needed something to be carried, like a washing machine, something that was heavy, then I would do that, together with the others who would be doing that that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you might be asked to carry a washing machine. Tell us more about that, please. Can you explain what's happening. Why would you have been asked to carry an item like a washing machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go to apartments and private homes that had been abandoned and simply carry out the things that were of any value.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And why did you do this? Is this something that you were told to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the soldiers who would take us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what unit did those soldiers belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit called ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This practice of going to apartments and private homes and carrying out things of value, is this something that occurred often or infrequently?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours. I object to the form of that question. It assumes facts not in evidence. That question states apartments and private homes when, in fact, Mr. Stringer just two questions about -- excuse me, the witness just two sentences ago stated on the record under oath these were abandoned. So how can they be private if they are abandoned? I object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, maybe you should lay more background for this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Tell us what you mean by "private homes," Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A house that's not an apartment building, but a house that just has one floor and an attic and a basement. Houses built by people out of their own funds, with their own resources. That's what I call private homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And getting back to my question, this practice of taking goods out of these private homes and apartments, how often did -- were you given this task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go many times, maybe five or six times, together with others. I spent more of my time in the headquarters, but I did go on such missions five or six times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know how frequently this practice occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. I know about the times that I went, and I know that things were transported in these trucks uphill above Mostar, and they ended up in the villages of Western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How do you know that these things ended up in the villages of Western Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go there and unload. I would pass there every day, from the Mostar Heliodrom, and I knew where that road went. And normally, before all these events, I would move along these roads, so I knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During those two months at the headquarters, how many prisoners would be taken to that place with you on those mornings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty to thirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What would happen to those prisoners upon their arrival at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would mostly stay in the headquarters, and a couple of other men. There were men working around the cars, the vehicles. There were those who went to the front line, the people who were attached to the command, should anything be needed. And one group went nonstop to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you're talking about prisoners now going to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Stela present when prisoners were sent to the front line or when prisoners engaged in looting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not present in the looting ever. As for going to the front line, he knew that prisoners were going to the front line. But I did not see him being present when the looting occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he aware that looting was taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers who were his subordinates would look for a couple of men to go and -- on these missions. Now, whether Stela knew that they were going looting or doing something else, I cannot ascertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Stela have a commander, a superior officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. He must have had, but I never saw him. I just heard that it was Mr. Tuta, whom I have never seen in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us about that? Where were you or how did you hear about Mr. Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were talking amongst themselves, that they had to go, had to contact him, but I did not see the man, nor did he come to see Stela while I was there. I didn't see him, nor did I ever know him or meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "they had to go" or "they had to contact him," do you know who would go or who would contact Stela, based on what you saw and heard in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this person that I didn't know, Tuta, how and why, I don't know. I'm just telling you what I heard. I didn't see the man. I didn't meet the man. I had no contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, Witness, my question is again based on what you saw and heard in the headquarters. Do you know who did have contact with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object. This question has been asked and answered. This witness does not know. He said it clearly two times. I object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I agree with you. Mr. Stringer, can you escape this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you testified about prisoners going to the front line, and I wanted to ask you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you if, again based on having worked in the headquarters those two months, you learned what was the zone or area of responsibility of this unit ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I also went there in due time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, taking the map again, which is Exhibit 11.18, I'm going to ask you to look at it, and if you can, perhaps just place two marks and what you consider to be the boundaries of the area of responsibility of this unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And for the record, Witness, I see that you've placed two blue marks which appear to delineate a section of the road that's called the Bulevar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only the line was 50 metres behind, in the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think to -- maybe to give an even better picture of the front line as far as you knew it to be, I'm going to ask the witness be shown Exhibits 14.3 and 14.4, two photographs. Okay. And I'll ask the witness just to take a look at them first, just so he can look at them well enough to become oriented. And then if he -- Witness, if you would -- if you can, on each of those photographs, can you place a mark which would again indicate what you believe to be the area of responsibility of the ATG Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. Thank you. Now, just for the record, you've made some markings on these two photographs. Would the area within these markings, would this correspond to the same area that you've marked on the map which is Exhibit 11.18?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We can set those aside now. On those occasions when you did go to the front line from the headquarters of ATG Mrmak, could you tell us the types of tasks that you were required to perform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If necessary, I would carry ammunition or something else for the soldiers on the front line, escorted by one of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what were the conditions in the areas in which you worked? Was it relatively safe or was it unsafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean -- are you referring to the prisoners who went to do work or you mean the separation line where the prisoners went to work or something else? I think that's...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, I think that's correct. When you and other prisoners went to work on what I think you called the front line, tell us, what were the conditions there in terms of whether it was dangerous or whether it was a safe place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. Every line is unsafe. People were getting killed on both sides, on any dividing line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not get any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has shown us a larger area without indicating the front line. Mr. President, the question by the Prosecutor is based on the assumption that the witness has told us where the line is, but the witness has shown us a larger area that does not indicate only the front line. So we don't know what the witness is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Maybe we could show this witness the photos again and ask the witness to draw a clear line of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Perhaps we could go with just one of the photographs. Perhaps we can work with Exhibit 14.4 to see whether that will be sufficient. And I would suggest, don't put any marks on the photo yet, okay. Let's put it on the ELMO for a minute and talk about it. I don't know about anyone else, but it would assist me if we could turn the photo 90 degrees to the left. Yes. And if we could just move it down a little bit so that the area that's already been marked by the witness is centered in the image that we're seeing. I think we can start to work that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let me ask you, first of all, when you went to work on the front line, in this photograph, are you able to point to any of the areas in which you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, this part of the building didn't exist at the time. Here, at the corner of this building, there was a bunker. Here, across the road, the road was barricaded with sandbags. To reach the line, you had to pass through the building, and the extreme end of the line was at the corner where there was a bunker. And then the line went up here along this way, up to about as far as this. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So the line is not something that ran along the Bulevar itself, but was, in fact, away from and to the west of the Bulevar among these buildings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we can try -- perhaps you could take a different pen. I see a green one next to your computer screen. And perhaps it would assist us if you could take that pen and, making a dotted line, simply indicate the confrontation line or the location of the bunkers and the fortifications which you've described.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Witness, when -- let me just take a step back. You've made marks on this photograph now in green, indicating the true front line, or the confrontation line in that area of the Bulevar. When you say you worked on the front line, are you saying that you worked in the area where you've made these green markings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What tasks did you perform, and other prisoners whom you worked with, what tasks were you prisoners performing in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bags were filled, bunkers had to be made, the area had to be cleaned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And when you were carrying out these tasks, were you in a position of risk in relation to the combatants, that is, the ABiH on one side and the HVO or the ATG Mrmak people on the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Mrmak ATG, that is, from their soldiers -- its soldiers were not a threat. The threat came from those on the other side, if those soldiers on the other side fired, perhaps, and they were in mutual conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So again just to be clear, could you describe the threat? What was the situation down there for you and the other prisoners who were working? What was the threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you walk, you are carrying those bags or making a bunker and there's fire all around, so naturally there's a good chance of being hit, just as many people were killed during these skirmishes whilst prisoners when they worked along the front lines throughout Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we'll talk about this in a little while. You were eventually wounded, but you were wounded working in a different area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I was wounded directly by a bullet, but my arm was injured. And I still suffer consequences because I was not extended proper medical aid at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And where did that -- where did you receive that injury? Where were you working at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Santiceva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to this photograph in this area that we're talking about, did you see any other prisoners or do you know of other prisoners who were injured while they were working in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to ask you about some things which would relate not to this area but to the headquarters of the ATG Mrmak. First of all, I want to ask you if you ever received beatings by anyone when you were working at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you describe that for us, please, and who beat you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ernest Takac beat me badly because I had to point all things green. And after that, he came and got me by my feet and hands and threw me out of the window of the room that I was working in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. We may have a little bit of a confusion in the transcript, so I just want to clarify that. You made a reference to "all things green," and I'm not sure it came through in my language. Can you describe what you mean by "all things green"? What is that about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had put on a green T-shirt, shorts, green -- everything was green, and green is the colour which is the symbol of Muslims. It is an Islamic colour, and therefore, all dressed in green, I was extra-extremist, extra -- somebody who is fond of green and all the rest, who loves Muslimhood above all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you put on these green clothes on your own or did someone else ask you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not do it for -- of my own will. I wouldn't do it today either. I have no -- I don't see what purpose that could serve.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, who told you to put on this green clothing while you were at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dinko and Ernest Takac, so that later on they could pull my leg. They could tease me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that Takac beat you badly and then threw you out of the window. Were you injured by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wounded? Well, to me, a wound comes from a bullet or something like that. So I was not wounded when that happened. I was beaten all over, but I wasn't wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Takac, Ernest Takac, have a gun or a pistol when he was beating you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't beat me with a pistol or a rifle. Of course he had a pistol behind his belt, but he was beating me with his fists and feet. He hit me some seven or eight times, because -- finally, I had to say, "I love green." And finally, he took out his pistol and said he'd kill me. He didn't do that. I stayed in that kitchen. I stayed behind in that kitchen and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did he do with the pistol when he drew it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He got me by my chin and said, I'll kill you, and then you won't love green or anything. And after that, he put the pistol back and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever observe Stela beat anyone or mistreat anyone at this headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once, when he hit a man who was -- whom people called "Professor" who had refused to obey to discard certain things that he had on him, that he had been given either by some friends or perhaps received by his family. He never laid a finger on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- this man, the professor, how old was he, if you know, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 50ish; 50, 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I did not see that man before or after that. Only some people who must have known him addressed him as "Professor, Professor," but I did not see him before or after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say that you saw Stela hit him. Did others see that incident; and if so, who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some -- there were a number of us there. As a matter of fact, we were all there because we were about to leave for the Heliodrom to board the truck. And the order was that nobody was to carry anything, and this one - I don't know why - refused to put down whatever he had, and Stela got that bag and threw it into a container and then pushed him, and pushed him into the garage that was next to that house. And in the garage, there was one of those pits, as they usually are in garages. And he was there for about half an hour, and then eventually he got ready and came to the Heliodrom with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was his condition when he came out of the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was all wet, because there was some water in that pit, or water came from outside. I don't know. But at any rate, he was soaked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd like for you to describe this pit and this garage. Do you know the purpose of the pit in this garage, what it was used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as in any other garage. There was a garage. And in the garage, there was a pit for car repair, that is, this hollow, a channel, we call it a pit, for car repair.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this is where a person could stand underneath a car and work with the car above him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly stand, but almost. A metre and 20 or so. That's how they usually build them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you know a prisoner named Seno Pajo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the question, because the examination is now moving in a direction necessitating answers which go beyond the scope of the indictment, and the only foundation for them could be perhaps a crime not covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this moment, we don't know where the Prosecutor is leading us. Mr. Stringer, would you give us some explanation about your direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I intend to lead the witness to another incident similar in some respects to the incident he just described. Every such incident is not alleged in the indictment but is certainly evidence of the intent of the accused, his willingness to mistreat prisoners in the presence of other prisoners and in the presence of his subordinates. And I simply intend to lead the witness to another incident which he witnessed with his own eyes at the headquarters. I believe very strongly that it is extremely relevant to the charges in the indictment, and it is not beyond the scope. I can go into greater detail and inform Your Honour exactly what I would like to lead, but I'm going to hold off just for the moment. Perhaps we can resolve this without my doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is a situation similar to the one we had last week when the Prosecutor started asking questions which could lead to establishing certain circumstances or facts which were questionable and which might indicate that a crime had been committed by the first accused. And the Chamber accepted the objection of Mr. Meek and suggested to the Prosecution to avoid the examination which would lead to adding charges which are not included in the indictment. I believe Mr. Stringer confirmed that I was right when he said that he was about to prove the intent of my client. Now, in view of the circumstances, or the choice -- I shouldn't like to talk about this before the witness. But nevertheless, the choice of a method or something could be pointing at the intent, and that intent is not a part of facts that is the substance of the crime which is -- with which my client is not charged in the present indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, we are only interested to hear the incidents that are charged in the indictment. And I think the Trial Chamber will make the conclusions about intent of the accused on those issues. So we'll give you the permission to continue, but only limit yourself to those incidents that are charged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I will indeed do that, Mr. President. The indictment very clearly charges that prisoners were mistreated, both on the front line and at the headquarters, and this is such an incident that falls squarely within the indictment, as well as being relevant to issues involving the intent of the accused, and again, issues regarding instigation of subordinates by committing misconduct and crimes in the presence of his subordinates. So in my view, Mr. President, and again, I know you're at a disadvantage because you don't know what we're about to lead, but I can only say that I very strongly disagree with counsel that this is something that somehow falls beyond the scope of the indictment. I also disagree with counsel's suggestion that there is something questionable or -- yes, "questionable" was the word that he used. I think, again it is your -- you are the Trial Chamber. You will decide what is questionable and what is not. In our view, it is an incident the witness will testify about from his personal knowledge, having seen it with his own eyes, and in our view, this is not anything that's is questionable and it falls well within the four corners of what is alleged in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, if we all together, who are here, including you, Your Honours, find in your indictment the name of the -- of this victim, then I will withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can respond, Mr. President, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, no, no, no. We are not debating this matter. We will give you some leeway for you to continue, but just bear in mind the strong objections from Defence counsel and the warning sent by this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you -- well, I did ask you if you knew another Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. prisoner named Seno Pajo. I don't know that I got your answer. Do you know such a prisoner or did you know such a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see any incidents involving that prisoner take place at the headquarters of ATG Mrmak, and if so, can you describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please go ahead and tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is precisely this situation that I'm talking about and because of which I objected, that is, the direction that the direct examination has taken or is taking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultations among the Judges, we believe that what we are going to hear will have some probative value, so we would like to hear what happened next. But bear in mind that this incident should be clearly stipulated in the indictment and be totally relevant to the counts listed in the indictment. Otherwise, this Trial Chamber will not take into consideration of that part of the testimony made by the witness. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, we've been discussing a witness. I've asked you about a witness named Pajo. You've said that you are aware of an incident which involved him at the headquarters. Could you tell us, please, what you saw, what happened in this incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seno Pajo was lying under the truck, repairing that truck, and from a package of grenades, Stela got one grenade, threw it through the window, and the shrapnel fragment of that grenade wounded Seno Pajo. But once again, it was -- it was a grenade which was thrown out of the window, not with the intent of wounding Seno. It was just thrown out randomly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where were you when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the office, because I had brought that package, that box of grenades, and I had taken it, unloaded it from the car which had brought that load of grenades, and I had taken it into that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you were present with Stela when he threw the grenade out the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then when we heard the scream, we both ran out, and Dolma and two or three other prisoners were already putting Seno in a car, and Dolma took him to the -- to Bijeli Brijeg, to the hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You said that you don't think it was the intent to injure that prisoner. If you know, what was the reason why the grenade was thrown out the window by Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: To test the grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Pajo was taken to the hospital by someone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I just wanted to make sure we have that name. Can you tell us again, please, the name of the person whom you said was putting him into the car to take him to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nino -- Nino, whose nickname was Dolma.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what was his rank or his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was, I think -- I mean, I think he was a commander of some unit or something. I don't think he was just a foot soldier, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the ATG Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was there. He went to the front line in that area. Now, I mean, I never looked at his military card. I never asked him if he belonged to that unit, but he went to the line which was within the -- which was the responsibility of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you -- Mr. President, I'm -- I might be able to finish before 4.00, I hope so, but I ask at this time to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
